blocks.text: Acme Scheduling scores as a feature, not a company.

Public course schedule and student planner for US colleges, fed by a one-way SQL export from the institution's student information system. No legal entity, founders, funding or headcount could be found; the domain was registered on 17 April 2026. Presumed founder-owned. Not a portfolio company.

Basis: 45 dated, sourced public facts gathered on 22 September 2026 (evidence log in Appendix B); scored against the nine-area v2.0 structure and weights. Bands: Resilient 8.5+, Solid 7.0 to 8.4, Thin 5.5 to 6.9, Eroding below 5.5. N/E = not evidenced; the weight is renormalised across evidenced drivers.

blocks.text: Reading

Acme Scheduling scores as a feature, not a company. It is a read-only presentation and analytics layer over the institution's student information system: data flows one way through a customer-run SQL export, the planner produces a shareable link rather than a registration, and the analytics are standard enrolment aggregations with CSV export [F11, F29, F33]. The status quo it replaces is a free static page [F3], SIS vendors already embed planners with registration write-back [F41], and a free consumer planner exists [F40].

The company itself is barely visible. The domain is five months old [F20]; three of four logos on the site are placeholders [F17]; the only real customer name still links its legacy schedule pages for Fall 2026 [F14-F16]; demo requests go to a webmail address [F22]; there is no privacy policy, terms of service, VPAT, SOC 2 or HECVAT [F23-F25], which US higher-education procurement usually requires.
What would prove this wrong

A very young product should not be expected to have renewals, certifications or reviews; the framework measures the moat that exists today, and a design partner deal with the named college may be live behind the legacy links.
Flat institutional pricing with a near-zero cost base is a workable micro-SaaS model; the framework's low score speaks to defensibility, not to whether the founder can make a living.
What moves the score

A registration hand-off or write-back into Banner, Colleague or Elements would move A3.1 from 1 to 5 and A2.5 from 1 to 5 (+0.3 in total). A VPAT, HECVAT and SOC 2 report would lift B2.3 from 0 to 5 (+0.16) and remove a procurement blocker.
Area findings

Each area shows its score out of 10, its weight in the headline and the share of its driver weight that public evidence allowed us to score. Bracketed references point to the evidence log in Appendix B.

blocks.title: Workflow & user replacement by AI agents
blocks.body: Users are the registrar's office, academic advisors, leadership viewers and students [F27, F42, F43]. Tiers cap admin users at 3 to 5, 25 and 50, so seat pressure appears as a tier downgrade rather than churn [F6, F8]. The analytics half is a reporting layer with CSV export and scheduled emails that an agent with SIS access reproduces [F4, F33].
blocks.counter: Students do not use agents to browse a schedule; the public page has a user population no automation removes.
blocks.gaps: Registrar and scheduling headcount trends; seats in use at the named college.

blocks.title: Data moat
blocks.body: First-party behavioural data (searches, filters, adds, conflicts) per institution surfaced as a Seat Demand Index and funnels [F30]; no cross-institution benchmark or data rights [F31]; at most one registration cycle of history [F20].
blocks.counter: Demand signals across many colleges would be novel; no SIS vendor publishes them.

blocks.title: Unit economics & inference margin
blocks.body: Serverless edge hosting and a static marketing site [F23, F25, F34]; no AI, so no inference cost; onboarding is a customer-run SQL push [F11]. Gross margin on a flat annual contract is close to the price.
blocks.counter: A near-zero cost base is a property of stage as much as of design; a real SIS integration would add support cost.
blocks.gaps: Hosting bill; support headcount; contract value at the named college.

blocks.text: Diligence questions for management

items: Which institutions are live on their own domain today, and which of the four logos are contracted customers?
Is a registration write-back into any SIS on the roadmap, and has any customer asked for it?
What compliance evidence (VPAT, HECVAT, SOC 2) exists or is in progress, and who owns it?
